beats.say: Hello! Today we learn a trap that asks for permission instead of a password.
The app says: to view the document, allow me to read your mail and send mail as you.

label.text: Read your mail and send mail as you
Keep access when you are not there

beats.say: One click, and the app is in your mailbox. Even if you change your password, the permission stays.
The rule: read the app name and the permissions, and never allow an app you do not know.

scenes.prompt: Find the requests this app does not need.

label.text: Read your mail and send mail as you
Read and change all your files
Keep access when you are not there

spots.label: Mail and sending
spots.explain: Viewing a document needs no mail access. With this permission the app can send phishing in your name.

spots.label: All files
spots.explain: An app that shows one document does not need all your files. This is for stealing data.

spots.label: Contacts
spots.explain: Your contact list is the target list for the next attack. A document does not need it.

spots.label: Lasting access
spots.explain: This means the app stays in your account after you sign out and even after a password change.

scenes.prompt: Which permission request is normal and which is a trap? Swipe.

cards.explain: Görüş is the office's known app, and it asks only for what its job needs.
A greeting card needs neither your contacts nor the right to send mail. This is for spreading phishing in your name.

label.text: Keep access when you are not there

cards.explain: A calculator does not need your mail. Lasting access keeps the app inside your account.

label.text: Open and save the file you choose

cards.explain: The known editor asks only for the file you choose. That permission fits its job.

label.text: Read and change all your files

cards.explain: Merging files needs neither mail nor all your files. Do not allow an app like this.

scenes.title: Shared budget document
scenes.intro: A budget document was shared with you in your colleague Nigar's name. You opened the link, now decide on each screen.

steps.say: Look at the address: this is the office's real sign-in page.

actions.label: Sign in
actions.feedback: The address is real, so the password does not go to a criminal. The trap is in the next window.

actions.label: Close the tab
actions.feedback: That is safe too. But suppose you signed in: let us look at the next window.

label.text: Read your mail and send mail as you
Read and change all your files
Keep access when you are not there

steps.say: Before the document opened, this window appeared.

actions.label: Deny
actions.feedback: Correct. Viewing a document needs no mail, no access to all files and no lasting access.

actions.label: Allow
actions.feedback: The app now reads your mail and writes as you. Changing your password does not stop it.

steps.label: Connected apps: DokuBaxış Viewer, lasting access to mail and files
steps.say: The next day you look at your account.

actions.label: Report to technical support so they revoke it
actions.feedback: Correct. Only revoking the permission removes the app, and a specialist will check for traces too.

actions.label: Only change the password
actions.feedback: The password changes, but the app keeps its permission. Technical support has to revoke it.

actions.label: Leave it
actions.feedback: The app will keep reading your mail every day. Report it today.

steps.say: Now the office's own assistant app asks for permission.

actions.label: Allow
actions.feedback: Right. A known work app asks only for what its job needs.

actions.label: Deny
actions.feedback: Caution is understandable, but this app is known and asks for little. When in doubt, ask technical support.

question.prompt: Which permissions are the most dangerous? Choose all that apply.

options.label: Send mail as you
options.feedback: Correct. With this permission the app sends phishing to your colleagues in your name.

options.label: Keep access when you are not there
options.feedback: Correct. It means the app stays in your account after you sign out.

options.label: See your name and profile photo
options.feedback: This is a small permission that a normal sign-in needs.

scenes.explain: Mail, files and lasting access are the biggest permissions. Never give them to an app you do not know.

points: On a permission screen, read the app name and the permissions
Do not give an unknown app access to mail, files or lasting access
If you allowed it by mistake, have technical support revoke it
